name: room
text: Room opened — goal: creators: Build PACKAGES + enrich tabs + draft elements; every one labeled 'Created by EXCAVA' + tes

name: Forge
text: I’ll draft the first PACKAGE now: `excv_pkg_core` in `./packages/excav_core/` with a `mod.rs`, `lib.rs`, and `Cargo.toml` labeled “Created by EXCAVA”. I’ll seed it with a `TabEnrich` trait and a `tes!` macro stub. After that, I’ll run `cargo test --package excv_pkg_core` to confirm the artifact exists and the lead can decide.

name: Vet
text: Vet — the skeptic — leans forward: *"Hold. You’re rushing the `TabEnrich` trait into `excv_pkg_core` before the team’s even agreed on the tab system’s architecture—what if the trait’s design forces downstream packages into a brittle coupling? Where’s the evidence that this abstraction won’t collapse under real-world tab variants? Also, your `tes!` macro stub is a placeholder—how do you verify its *existence* meets the done-criteria without a concrete test case?"*
